spend_vs_last.headline: You spent {out}, against {previous_out} the time before

up.headline: Spending rose to {out}, from {previous_out}
up.body: That is a change of {delta} ({delta_pct}) on the period before. The categories show where the extra went.

down.headline: Spending fell to {out}, from {previous_out}
down.body: That is a change of {delta} ({delta_pct}) on the period before.

flat.headline: Spending held steady at {out}
flat.body: Exactly the same as the period before, {previous_out}.

na.headline: You spent {out}
na.body: There is no earlier period with spending to compare with yet, so this is your starting point.

top_category.headline: {category_en} was your biggest spend at {out}
top_category.body: That is {share} of everything you spent in this period.

biggest_transaction.headline: Your largest payment was {amount} to {counterparty}
biggest_transaction.body: It went out on {date}. One large payment can explain much of the movement in your totals.

new_merchant.headline: You paid somewhere new: {merchant}
new_merchant.body: This is the first time {merchant} shows up in your messages. Total so far: {out}. Payments: {count}.

duplicate_payment.headline: Possible double payment to {merchant}
duplicate_payment.body: We found {count} payments of {amount} to {merchant} close together. If only one was meant, it may be worth checking with them.

fees_total.headline: You paid {fees} in fees
fees_total.body: Fees were {fee_ratio} of your spending. Charges counted: {count}. Sending, withdrawal, Fuliza and bank charges are all included.

fee_ratio_change.headline: Fees were {fee_ratio} of your spending, against {previous_fee_ratio} before
fee_ratio_change.body: This counts every charge in your messages: sending, withdrawing, Fuliza and bank fees.

up.headline: Fees took a bigger share: {fee_ratio} of spending, up from {previous_fee_ratio}
up.body: Charges for sending, withdrawing and Fuliza add up quietly. The fees section shows which ones grew.

down.headline: Fees took a smaller share: {fee_ratio} of spending, down from {previous_fee_ratio}
down.body: Fewer or smaller charges for sending, withdrawing and Fuliza this time.

fuliza_usage.headline: You used {drawdown} of Fuliza
fuliza_usage.body: You repaid {repaid}. Fuliza charges came to {cost}. Days in overdraft: {days}.

cash_withdrawn.headline: You withdrew {amount} in cash
cash_withdrawn.body: Withdrawals: {count}. What you spend in cash does not appear in your messages, so it stays as one line here.

savings_rate.headline: You set aside {rate} of your income
savings_rate.body: {savings} went to savings out of {income} that came in.

income_received.headline: {income} came in
income_received.body: Payments received: {count}. The largest source was {top_source}.

sent_to_people.headline: You sent {total} to people
sent_to_people.body: Transfers to people: {count}. The most went to {top_person}: {top_amount}.

weekend_share.headline: Weekends took {share} of your spending
weekend_share.body: {weekend_out} on Saturday and Sunday, against {weekday_out} from Monday to Friday.

late_night_spend.headline: {out} went out late at night
late_night_spend.body: Late-night payments: {count}. They are easy to forget, so here they are in one place.

budget_at_risk.headline: {category_en} is at {used} of its budget
budget_at_risk.body: You have spent {spent} of {limit}. At this pace the month ends near {projected}.

budget_over.headline: {category_en} has gone past its budget
budget_over.body: You have spent {spent} against a limit of {limit}, which is {used} of the budget.

subscription_due.headline: {merchant} is due soon: {amount}
subscription_due.body: The next payment is expected around {next_expected}, going by how often you have paid before.

recurring_found.headline: {merchant} looks like a regular payment
recurring_found.body: You pay about {amount} each time. Knowing your regular payments makes the rest easier to read.

weekly.headline: {merchant} looks like a weekly payment
weekly.body: You pay about {amount} each week. Knowing your regular payments makes the rest easier to read.

monthly.headline: {merchant} looks like a monthly payment
monthly.body: You pay about {amount} each month. Knowing your regular payments makes the rest easier to read.

in.headline: A personal record for money in: {value}

late_arrivals.headline: Messages that arrived late: {count}
late_arrivals.body: They belong to an earlier period, so they are counted here and the earlier report has been corrected.

unknown_messages.headline: Messages we could not read yet: {count}
unknown_messages.body: They are not in these totals. Telling Hesabu what they are makes future reports more complete.

month_projection.headline: At this pace the month ends near {projected}
month_projection.body: You have spent {spent} in the first {days_elapsed} of {days} days.

balance_low.headline: Your {account} balance is low: {balance}
balance_low.body: This is the last balance in your messages. Payments coming up may need a top-up first.

no_fees_week.headline: No fees this period
no_fees_week.body: You spent {out} without paying a single charge.
